title: Self-Refine and CRITIC: Iterative Output Improvement

questions.question: What three prompts make up a Self-Refine loop?
options: Generate, feedback, refine
Plan, execute, solve the task
Actor, evaluator, reflector
Search, score, synthesize
questions.explanation: Self-Refine uses one model in three roles: generate, feedback, refine.

questions.question: Why does Self-Refine require history on the refine step?
options: Because most providers only apply prompt caching to prompts that carry history
Without prior outputs and critiques the refine step repeats earlier mistakes
Because the refine step needs history to bill the call at the right token rate
Including history in the refine prompt speeds up token generation noticeably
questions.explanation: The refine prompt conditions on the full history so the model does not repeat its earlier errors.

questions.question: What does CRITIC change relative to Self-Refine?
options: It drops the refine step entirely and stops after the first critique
It swaps in a larger model for the generation step while feedback stays the same
It replaces the self-feedback step with an external tool-grounded verifier
It runs the feedback and refine steps in parallel instead of in sequence
questions.explanation: CRITIC swaps self-critique for a verify step routed through search, code interpreter, calculator, or domain verifiers.

questions.question: Which Anthropic workflow pattern matches Self-Refine and CRITIC in Claude-friendly language?
options: Router - classify the request, then dispatch it to a specialist prompt
Prompt chain - a fixed sequence of prompts run one after another
Parallel sampling - run several generations at once and pick the best one
Evaluator-Optimizer - score the output, then revise it and loop
questions.explanation: Anthropic names this pattern Evaluator-Optimizer: an evaluator scores, an optimizer revises, loop until convergence.

questions.question: What is a rubber-stamp loop and how does the lesson recommend avoiding it?
options: A test that always passes, fixed by removing that test from the suite entirely and moving on
Same model, same prompt critiquing its own output; use different prompts or a smaller separate critic instead
A retry that always fails, fixed by raising the retry budget much higher than before
A guardrail that keeps timing out, fixed by widening its timeout window considerably
questions.explanation: Same-style self-critique converges on 'looks good to me'; differentiate the evaluator from the optimizer.

questions.question: Which SDK feature in OpenAI Agents SDK is CRITIC-shaped?
options: Handoffs, which transfer a conversation to a different specialist agent
Sessions, which persist conversation state across separate agent runs
Output guardrails, which validate the final output and can call tools
Tracing, which records spans for every step of an agent run
questions.explanation: Output guardrails validate the final agent output and can call tools, matching CRITIC's verifier role.
